notes: Built from 24 TaskTrove Clean discovery tasks.
All units are candidates until the evidence rubric passes.
Empty micro_area_ids indicate that the broad inventory has no honest micro-area match.

units.name: Evaluate numeric expressions with signed values
units.outcome: Evaluate numeric expressions containing negative values, grouping, and mixed arithmetic operations while preserving sign and operation precedence.
includes: Adding and subtracting signed integers
Applying precedence in mixed-operation numeric expressions
Evaluating nested groups with signed intermediate values
excludes: Symbolic manipulation of expressions with unknown variables
positive_examples: Evaluate an expression with negative factors and mixed operations
Evaluate a parenthesized expression before applying an outer multiplier

units.name: Filter finite integer candidates by arithmetic conditions
units.outcome: Construct a finite set of integer candidates, apply all stated digit, divisibility, or primality conditions, and count the candidates that remain.
includes: Enumerating an inclusive integer interval
Generating bounded candidates from digit constraints
Testing candidate integers for primality
Counting candidates satisfying several simultaneous conditions
excludes: Counting structures defined by pairings or permutations
positive_examples: Count primes in a specified finite interval
Count three-digit primes whose digits satisfy an equation
Enumerate bounded digit tuples, construct their integers, and retain only prime candidates

units.name: Compute integer powers modulo a modulus
units.outcome: Compute the least nonnegative residue of a large integer power by using repeated squaring, congruence structure, or periodicity instead of evaluating the unreduced power.
includes: Translating terminal-digit questions into modular arithmetic
Reducing large powers by repeated squaring or periodicity
Exploiting structure specific to the base and modulus
Returning a least nonnegative residue or fixed-width terminal digits
excludes: General symbolic exponent manipulation without a modulus
positive_examples: Find the final three decimal digits of a large power
Identify and use a repeating residue pattern to reduce an exponent

units.name: Derive triangle measurements from equivalent descriptions
units.outcome: Derive a requested triangle length, area, radius, or altitude by converting the supplied coordinates or side information into an equivalent metric relation.
includes: Computing side lengths from vertex coordinates
Computing triangle area from coordinates or perpendicular sides
Relating area to semiperimeter and inradius
Relating area to a side and its corresponding altitude
excludes: Optimizing over a family of feasible triangles
Counting lines, tangencies, or other geometric configurations
positive_examples: Find a triangle's inradius from its vertex coordinates
Find the altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle
Equate two area formulas to recover an unknown triangle measurement

units.name: Optimize geometric quantities under constraints
units.outcome: Translate geometric feasibility conditions into a parameterized objective and admissible domain, then determine an extremal geometric value.
includes: Expressing an area or distance as an objective
Deriving admissibility conditions from side, intersection, or distance constraints
Optimizing over the admissible configurations
Checking that the proposed extremum corresponds to a feasible configuration
excludes: Computing one fixed triangle measurement without optimization
Counting admissible configurations without an objective
Unconstrained symbolic optimization with no geometric model
positive_examples: Maximize triangle area subject to independent side-length bounds
Maximize the area determined by a line's intersections with an ellipse
Optimize a triangle quantity subject to excircle constraints
Minimize a complex-modulus expression by interpreting it as planar distance

units.name: Count structures built from fixed points and pairs
units.outcome: Count finite structures that decompose into disjoint fixed points and unordered pairs by enumerating feasible decompositions and avoiding duplicate representations.
includes: Choosing any unpaired or fixed elements
Counting pairings of the remaining labeled elements
Representing involutions as fixed points and disjoint transpositions
Separating cases by the number of pairs
excludes: Classifying subgroups of a permutation group
positive_examples: Count pairings of five labeled objects with one object left unpaired
Count self-inverse functions by decomposing them into fixed points and transpositions
Count labeled arrangements composed only of singleton and two-element blocks
